- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp spikes or high volatility periods.
- Underestimate during prolonged low-price phases or when historical mean reversion is evident.
- Overshoot after sudden price spikes; model tends to overreact and fail to correct downward quickly.
- Lag in response to true price drops; model often holds higher values longer than actuals.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices in the first 5–10 days of forecast, then gradually adjusts.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., after 40+ days of high prices), model fails to reflect this trend.
- Forecast tends to ignore or underweight extreme outliers (e.g., 34.33 or 32.56) in favor of smoother trends.
- Model overfits recent high prices, leading to overconfidence in upward momentum even when fundamentals suggest otherwise.
